50:2.4.1.text: Gull. The east end. The far end is a real place.
50:2.4.1.when: When: The player arrives in Gull's east bay holding the lock-2 keys (the far end inks; bible 5.3.4)

50:2.4.2.text: A white stone on a stump at the dam. His sign.
50:2.4.2.when: When: They see the white stone and the stone is understood

50:2.4.3.text: That pipe at the dam is drill rod. Somebody set it there for a canoe.
50:2.4.3.when: When: They hold Tauno's crew-gear talk and see the rod in fall

50:2.4.4.text: He set the same stone under the paddle at Pietro. Same hand.
50:2.4.4.when: When: They have seen the paddle-stone at Pietro and land here

50:3.1.w.blaze.text: Orange on the blazes. Crew line. Tauno said.

50:4.3.w.boots.text: His boots are under the cot. Muddy.

50:4.3.w.corebox.text: The core boxes say E-7. This is where they drilled. Not Pietro.

50:4.3.w.sun.text: A sun pencilled on the back door. The door faces the Christmas sunrise. He hung it that way.

50:4.3.w.floor.text: The missing pages. He tore them out of the notebook and left them under his own stone.

50:4.4.w.pages.text: He carried them up in the rain with his brother. 'Saturday.' Where V. dug, toward the Christmas sunrise. He wanted it in a newspaper.

note.june.text:
W —
Coffee's in the blue can, not the red one.
The red one is nails. You know this.
Back Sunday.
— J.

50:4.5.w.june.text: A note from June, behind the photo. He kept it twenty-some years and brought it up here.

50:4.6.w.marks.text: He marked every October here. The last one is '17.

50:4.6.w.tally.text: 50, 63, 121, 214. The back cover again. He ticked two. The dry bag and the Grumman.

50:5.2.frozen.text: Frozen in. Not till the ice goes.

note.eino.text:
W. — Saturday.
Bring the good coffee.
Eino.

50:5.3.w.eino.text: Eino's note, on top of the cans. 'Saturday.' They were coming back for them together.

50:6.7.w.paddle.text: The fifty off the back door. His stone, his paddle.

scanner.quiet.1.text: One. Nothing moving. Dark as a pocket in here.

scanner.quiet.2.text: Take your time, fellas. He's got all night and so have we.

scanner.quiet.3.text: Nobody gets wet. Nobody gets loud. We just want to say hello.

scanner.quiet.4.text: Two. On the water at the landing. Going up.

scanner.quiet.6.text: Everybody keep your lights low till you need them.

scanner.noticed.1.text: Two. Light at the south end. Was. It's gone.

scanner.noticed.2.text: Something on the water off the point. Could be a loon.

scanner.noticed.4.text: Loons just went up behind me.

scanner.seen.2.text: Got him. Clearwater, west of the island. He's going for the long one.

scanner.seen.3.text: Two, sit on the Rock Island end. He has to come by you.

scanner.seen.4.text: He's on Gull, past the burnt point. No light.

scanner.seen.5.text: Three, go round by Turtle. Take your time. He's not going anywhere fast with that load.

scanner.lost.2.text: Then sit still and listen. Nobody paddles all night without making noise.

scanner.lost.3.text: He'll have to come out on a landing sometime. Sit on the landings.

scanner.day.1.text: One. I've got him. Broad daylight. He's just sitting there.

scanner.day.2.text: Then we sit too. Everybody on the landings. Nobody goes near him on the water.

then.text: Then get in the lee. He will.

scanner.denny.1.text: Our friend says the river. Three, go up the river.

scanner.denny.2.text: Three. Nothing on the river. Nothing all night.

scanner.feint.1.text: Light on the narrows. He's going west. Bald Eagle.

scanner.feint.2.text: All right. Three, stay on the narrows. One, go on over behind him.

scanner.feint.3.text: He's playing with you, fellas. Sit on both.
scanner.feint.3.if: if the player then goes north

scanner.dawn.1.text: Two, go home and sit off the landing.

scanner.dawn.2.text: Two. Going home. Nothing in the islands.

scanner.dawn.3.text: I'm on the landing. Nobody comes past me in the dark.
scanner.dawn.3.how: 05:00, as his flashlight comes on at the landing

scanner.dawn.4.text: Fog's in. Can't see my own bow.

scanner.dawn.5.text: Party pulling in. I'm going up to the truck. Two, you sit.

scanner.dawn.6.how: if the player reaches the lot

50:8.4.1.text: Morning. Just waiting on a friend.

50:8.4.3.text: I don't go in the water.

50:9.1.c3.text: [Say nothing. Set the cans on the tailgate.]

50:9.1.2.text: 'Re: Haapala, E.' 'If he persists, D.S. will handle it.' Six weeks before.

50:9.1.3.text: This doesn't say who was on the lake that morning. I want you to know I know that. It says enough.

50:9.1.c4.text: There was a note on top.

50:9.1.4.text: Keep that. That's not evidence. That's his.

50:9.1.5.text: Who wrote me in 2019? The letter, Ely postmark. I need the source. I'm not asking where. I'm asking who.

50:9.1.7.text: Then that's the story. The man who wrote me, the canoe on the wrong shore, the men who watched him. His name goes in. Once it's in print, it's in print.

50:9.1.c8.text: Somebody who knew the family. That's all I can give you.

50:9.1.9.text: A source who knew the Haapala family. Bill's box carries '77. It's thinner. It'll hold.

50:9.1.10.text: Okay. Neither do I. We'll say that.

50:9.1.11.text: Go home. Sleep in a bed. I'll call your counter when it's running. You did the hard part. I just type.

50:9.1.14.text: I'd have paid you. You know that? Whatever it was.

50:9.1.17.text: Somebody called the paper about a pack and two cans. Maggie Tomczak, the Ledger. That you?

paper.ledger.j.text:
THE NORTHLAND LEDGER

STATIONS 7 TO 12
Field books hidden in 1977 show a mining company relabelled a polluted creek
as "background." The man whose initials are on the change advises Northmark today.

By Maggie Tomczak

In August 1976, after two days of rain, the creek below Boreal Range Minerals'
Kettle pad ran orange for a kilometre and killed the fish in it. Three crewmen
took the readings. A month later, the company's exploration manager pencilled
six sampling stations out of the "below pad" column of its state water report
and into "background." His initials, C.B., are on the draft.

Carl Brekke, 88, was Boreal's exploration manager from 1972 to 1984. He is now
senior technical advisor to Northmark Metals, whose Kettle project rests on a
water baseline built from Boreal's 1976 and 1977 filings. He did not respond
to questions.

The papers -- four original field books, the pencilled draft, a cash ledger
and a 1977 company memo -- were found this fall by a canoeist carrying a
guide's old gear from the back room of {home outfitter}. The ledger records
two years of cash paid to a state water inspector and a county commissioner,
both since dead, named only by initials.

The memo, dated 30 August 1977, concerns a crew water sampler, Eino Haapala.
It says he "has been spoken to" about the field books. Six weeks later he
drowned on Bald Eagle Lake. The memo does not say what happened to him.
Nothing else the Ledger has seen does either.

{Walt named:} The papers were hidden by Eino and his brother, Walter Haapala,
a guide who was presumed drowned on Birch Lake in 2019. Sources say he did not
drown. In 2019 he wrote to this reporter, unsigned, and told her where to look.

{Kept:} A source who knew the Haapala family helped the Ledger confirm the
papers. A 1977 note by the late Duluth reporter Bill Ostrander records that
Eino Haapala had arranged to meet him two days after he disappeared.

{Tauno on record:} "We took the readings and they changed them," said Tauno
Kangas, 81, of Ely, a Boreal crew chief in 1976. "I recopied three days of it
myself. I've been sorry fifty years."

{Not on record:} A former Boreal crewman confirmed the readings.

Northmark said in a statement that it "takes these historical questions
seriously" and will review its baseline.

50:9.1.18.text: Fifty years I watched that lot for him.
50:9.1.18.if: to nobody, or to the player if they are near the porch

50:9.2.1.text: Two hundred fifty thousand. Twenty-five today, here. The rest as consulting fees, a little every time you come out of the woods. That's how legal wanted it. I don't know why. I think it's a tax thing.

50:9.2.2.text: Old exploration data. Company property. A liability if it comes out wrong, is what they tell me. I believe them. You think I shouldn't?

50:9.2.3.text: And nobody goes looking for the old fella any more. Wherever he is. That one's on me.

50:9.2.c7.if: to Maggie's wagon or the bench; nobody stops the player.

50:9.2.4.text: Thank you. Did you read them?
50:9.2.4.if: holding out his hand; the heavy gold ring

50:9.2.5.text: Then you know what it cost.

50:9.2.7.text: You knew the station numbers. And you came to us anyway. First sensible thing anybody near that family's done in fifty years.

50:9.2.8.text: It's only old paper. But it's ours. Walt was the best line-cutter I ever had.

paper.column.m.text:
THE NORTHLAND LEDGER — NORTHERN NOTEBOOK

The papers existed.

For two years I have been asking about water readings a mining company filed
with the state in 1976. This fall I learned that the original field books
existed, and a good deal else besides. They were found by someone using old
gear from the back room of {home outfitter}.

They were sold.

I don't know the price. I hope it was a lot.

-- Maggie Tomczak

50:11.1.text: Hey, so, this came for you. I think? It says 'To the one with my tent.' That's you, right? There's no name on it. There's a little drawing. Canada. Atikokan. Do you know anybody in Atikokan?

50:11.4.text: Two cups this morning. Drank both.
50:11.4.when: Ending: Journalist, Walt kept out of print

50:11.5.text: Saw my name in the paper. Moving on before the snow. Glad it's out.

50:11.6.text: Saw they got their permit. Hope it bought you something good. Keep your canoe close.

50:12.3.c1.text: I found this on top of them.

50:12.3.1.text: Eighth of August. Sawbill. You're buying.

50:12.3.2.text: I wanted the mine. I still want the mine. Now it's a fair fight.

50:12.3.4.text: I wanted the mine. Not like this. They're building it on a lie, and they paid you for the lie.

50:12.3.5.text: Thank you. I'm sorry. Both. — D.
50:12.3.5.when: *Turned:* journalist: he sends a card to the home counter

50:12.3.6.text: I read it. The paper. I read it in the car three times.

50:12.3.7.text: Somebody talked, back then. I always thought somebody talked.

50:12.3.8.text: I hope it was a lot.
50:12.3.8.when: *Money:* if the player talks to her again

50:12.3.9.text: Somebody left an old Grumman at the {landing}. Boss says it's ours now. It's loud but it's basically indestructible.
50:12.3.9.if: Only if the player used the Grumman; it goes on the home rental rack, and from then on now and then a family party is seen paddling it: "Some kid'll need it someday."

50:12.4.1.text: Paper says the papers were in the woods somewhere back of Bald Eagle. Didn't say where. I'm not asking where. If there was anything else back there. A building, say. Is it history or junk? I'm supposed to know which.

50:12.4.2.text: Okay. I never heard about it.

50:12.4.3.text: Then tell me where, sometime, and I'll come with a crew.
